stem:
Lata tracks a number trick with one letter-number $x$ for the starting number, kept the same in every step: multiply by $4$, add $12$, divide by $4$, then subtract the starting number.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims correctly describe what this tracking shows?

options.text: The expression simplifies to $3$, so every starting number gives the final result $3$.
$x$ is only a label for letter-number, so it cannot appear in the arithmetic steps.
Keeping the same $x$ through every step shows the final result is fixed for every starting number.
She must also use a right-triangle length rule to finish the proof.

teacher.key_rationale: (4x+12)/4 - x = x+3 - x = 3, so the result is always 3 when the same x is kept. Treating x as a mere unused label swaps the role of the letter-number. Bringing in a triangle length rule leaves the hinge.
